messages:
maria: quick heads-up — in staging I saw requests from workspace A getting routed to the dedicated egress pool for workspace B when X-Workspace header was absent. repro steps below.

ajay: do you have the request sample + gateway logs?

maria: yep. minimal repro: POST /v1/generate with tenant token for A but no X-Workspace header. gateway picked pool: pool-dedicated-b.

```
req id=rc_9f3a content: {"model":"r-infer/7b","input":"hello"}
auth workspace: workspace-A
headers: { Authorization: Bearer, Host: api.prod.redwood, X-Workspace: <missing> }
route decision: matched pool=pool-dedicated-b by header-eject-rule
```

kevin: oof. sounds like our header-ejection rule is treating missing as wildcard. current priority table: explicit workspace header > workspace-from-token > pool-affinity, but missing header flows to header-eject fallback which picks any compatible dedicated pool.

sam: is this limited to dedicated pools or also private VPC endpoints?

maria: mostly dedicated so far. I saw one spike where private-endpoint routing also accepted the request because token-scoped check ran later than header rule.

ajay: two issues to fix: 1) ensure missing X-Workspace is treated as "no header" (no eject), not wildcard; 2) short-circuit token-scoped workspace assert before pool assignment.

lee: agree. Ops concern: changing evaluation order might increase cold-fallbacks when customers rely on header hinting for multi-workspace tokens. Need telemetry to understand how many requests rely on header vs token for routing.

kevin: proposal: new ordered policy: 1) if X-Workspace present -> assert and route; 2) else evaluate token workspace binding -> if bound -> route; 3) else evaluate pool-affinity (shared/dedicated) but only choose dedicated pools that explicitly list "allow-unknown-workspace": true. default dedicated pools must be opt-in.

sam: that addresses safety. we also need a console UX to flag dedicated pools with that opt-in toggle + clear tooltip about "opt into accepting requests with missing workspace header".

maria: logging/telemetry: add fields route_hint_source=[header|token|pool-default] and pool_selection_reason=[explicit|fallback|mismatch-eject]. Emit both to route-decisions trace span; then we can graph traffic that would've been ejected vs accepted.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: ENGPLAT-4821. Add unit tests for header missing behavior, integration test with token-scoped assert, migration plan for existing dedicated pools.

ajay: dev plan: I'll open PR to change evaluator order + require allow-unknown flag on dedicated pools. Maria can add telemetry/trace changes. Kevin to update pool schema and console toggle. Sam to draft rollout notes and canary gates.

kevin: ETA?

ajay: PR today for evaluator change, tests tomorrow. canary for 48h.

maria: I'll start a short eval that replays 24h staging traffic to estimate how many would flip.

lee: add a temporary reject-count alert (non-prod) for misrouted requests so we can detect regressions during canary.

sam: for console rollout UX: add a per-pool checkbox "accept requests without workspace header" + a prominent warning. I'll mock in Figma and post link.

maria: thanks all — I'll post the trace sample after replay. :thumbsup:
